beats.intro: Lesson thirteen. [[sub]]What planning really produces, and how objectives and key results turn it into daily work.
beats.output: What does planning produce? [[tasks]]Tasks done now, to change what happens later. [[past]]Many people spot today's gap and rush to decide how to fix it. But today's gap is a failure of planning in the past. [[gas]]It is like scrambling after the car has already run out of gas. [[q]]The planning question is: what do I have to do today to solve, or better, avoid, tomorrow's problem? [[book]]Grove hardly ever opened the bound annual plan. The output was the actions it prompted.
beats.horizon: How far ahead? [[five]]Intel planned five years out every year. [[one]]But what that really shapes is the next year, and only the next year. [[roll]]A year later you plan again, and year two becomes year one. [[only]]So act only on the part of the plan before your next planning cycle. [[often]]But don't plan too often, either. You need time to see whether your last decisions were right.
beats.who: Who should plan? [[ops]]The managers who will carry the plan out. [[apart]]Planners working apart from the people implementing simply does not work. [[lev]]Planning has enormous leverage, but only when it is married to implementation. [[yes]]And remember: every yes is a no to something else. [[drop]]Planners need the guts and the discipline to drop projects as well as start them.
beats.mbo: Management by objectives applies planning to daily work. [[short]]Over a short horizon you already know what is demanded, so it concentrates on steps two and three, and makes them specific. [[road]]As the old saying goes, if you don't know where you're going, any road will get you there. [[two]]It answers two questions. [[obj]]Where do I want to go? That is the objective. [[kr]]How will I pace myself to see if I am getting there? Those are the key results.
beats.airport: Say you must reach the airport for a flight in an hour. [[obj]]That is the objective. [[a]]On the way are towns A, B and C, [[times]]which you should reach at ten, twenty and thirty minutes. [[lost]]If you have driven twenty minutes and haven't reached town A, you know you are lost. [[ask]]Get off the highway and ask for directions, or you'll miss the flight.
beats.period: Key results are feedback, and feedback works only if it comes soon after the work. [[short]]So keep the period short. [[q]]With a yearly plan, set objectives quarterly, or even monthly.
beats.focus: Above all, objectives should give focus. [[few]]That only works if there are few of them. [[many]]In practice we can't say no, and the list grows. [[nothing]]Focus on everything, and you focus on nothing. [[clear]]A few well-chosen objectives say clearly what you are saying yes to, and what you are saying no to.
beats.columbus: Grove tells Columbus's story, taking liberties with the schoolbook version. [[plan]]Spain's planning for 1491 showed it couldn't fund the war it was fighting without more money. [[isa]]Queen Isabella's objective: increase Spain's wealth through trade. [[talk]]She and Columbus discussed options freely, and reached a clear decision: [[route]]his objective would be to find a new route to the Orient. [[krs]]His key results: get ships, train crews, make a shakedown cruise, set sail, each with a deadline. [[nest]]The objectives nest: if his are met, hers will be too.
beats.missed: Columbus hit every key result, [[miss]]and missed the objective. There was no new route to China. [[found]]But he found the New World, a source of enormous wealth for Spain. [[well]]So a person can perform well while missing a stated objective. [[stop]]The system is a stopwatch in your own hand, to pace yourself. [[legal]]It is not a legal document for a performance review. [[petty]]A manager who rates people mechanically by it, or a report who ignores an opportunity because it wasn't on the list, is being petty and unprofessional.
beats.plant: Back to the Philippine plant. [[obj]]The Far East construction manager's objective: obtain a decision on the plant expansion. [[k1]]Key result one: study land near the plant and elsewhere, by June. [[k2]]Two: financial analyses of land, construction and operating costs for both sites. [[k3]]Three: present to the steering group and get its decision. [[k4]]Four: Grove ratifies by October. [[met]]Every key result was met, and so was the objective. [[spec]]Notice how specific they are. At the deadline, there's no doubt whether each was done.
beats.nest: His boss had an objective too: keep all plant expansions on schedule. [[kr]]One of the boss's key results: get the Philippine decision by October, much like his subordinate's objective. [[link]]Objectives link up the chain, as Isabella's and Columbus's did. [[judge]]But it can't be run mechanically. Setting objectives and key results takes judgment and common sense. [[okr]]A note beyond the book: Grove's objectives and key results are widely seen as the origin of today's OKRs.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]Planning's output is what you do today about tomorrow. [[w2]]Plan years ahead, but act only until your next planning cycle. [[w3]]The people who implement must plan, and must drop things too. [[w4]]Objectives say where; key results, few, short and specific, pace you. [[w5]]Key results are a stopwatch, not a legal document. Now the lesson practice.

beats.finish: Well done. That is the end of lesson thirteen, and of part three, on deciding and planning.
